# `ScopeTrack`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Mount tracking switched on or off.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER (observation only; receiving the event changes nothing) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, SendTrackEvent @0x412d0, CheckTrackState @0x41be0, getTrackReason @0xf1770 (64-bit guider build); 32-bit counterpart present |

Custom guider producer (not S or F). Sent by the guider's tracking-state check on tracking transitions, including the forced check after scope_set_track_state (whether the controller command succeeded or not) and checks reached from coordinate reads and from slew completion. The check stores the last tracking flag and code and emits only when one of them changes, so there is no periodic tracking timer; a reader (a tracking or coordinate getter, goto arrival, or the imager's focus and position polling) drives the emission. When not tracking, the fault code is the mount controller's tracking reason mapped by the guider, 270 (below horizon), 527 (alt exceed limit), 203 during a home or horizon move, or 207 (fail to operate) for a reply the guider does not recognise; the below-horizon decision is the controller's, not a guider altitude computation. Emitted by the guider on TCP 4400 to every retained socket; the main imager process forwards the line unchanged onto TCP 4700 (the auxiliary imager process suppresses guider forwarding). The event can precede the reply to the command that caused it; order is not established. The APK's generic state mapper does not know on/off; its tracking branch reads the tracking member.

Side effects: None for the receiver; the device sends this without a request.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"ScopeTrack"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string <seconds>.<nine digits> from clock id 1 (monotonic, INFERRED); not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `state` | string | yes | - | on or off. One of: `on`, `off`. [READ] |
| `tracking` | boolean | yes | - | Tracking state. [READ] |
| `manual` | boolean | yes | - | Manual-transition flag (set when a tracking command forced the check). [READ] |
| `error` | string | if positive fault code | - | Fault message. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | if positive fault code | - | Fault code, only when positive. [READ] |
| `route` | array<string> | if a named parent function is active | - | Function ancestry when a named parent is active. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, on - Tracking enabled by a command (READ shape):

```json
{"Event":"ScopeTrack","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"on","tracking":true,"manual":true}
```

Event, off-below-horizon - Tracking off below the horizon (READ shape; code and text from the error table):

```json
{"Event":"ScopeTrack","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"off","tracking":false,"manual":false,"error":"below horizon","code":270}
```
